Nadeem: No, that's Nadeem not Nadine, and only 20% of Nadeems will want to fight you if you repeatedly call him that. As a rule, Nadeem is a gentle sound for a forgiving and friendly man. But yes, like many Middle Eastern men, if you question his parentage he'll lose the smile and shape up immediately. (He is therefore not the person to be Earth's rep when/if we finally meet some curious extraterrestrials.)
Naren: Across between Norm and Karen, Naren is a contented and humble soul and quite possibly another accomplished artist who is doing his bit.
Nariano: Nariano is one of the few men in the Kingdom who is just about sick and tired of women throwing themselves at him.
Nash: The lock-picker who smiles all day and all night.
Nat: No, Nat isn't going to spend hours in deep discussions about the philosophy of any particular decision. If it feels right he’ll do it, if it doesn’t he won’t and the past is the past - this about sums him up. To sit around and talk about the ins and outs of why or why not something happened will only bore him shitless. By the way, don't deem him to be impulsive just because he moves and acts faster than you. It's just how he is. He's a hands-on dude, simple as that. Girls love him in his younger years because they think he's reckless, and he'll milk that idea for all its worth too, don't you worry, even though that isn't true either. He's no fool.
Nate: Deliberately eats food that makes him fart a lot.
Nathan: Usually blonde, Nathan is one of the Achievers. Anal and organised, his only real problem is that he wears underpants that are too small, which results in lots of frowning when he smiles.
Nathaniel: It probably won’t ever happen – I mean, how many people actually get to save the world – but if someone had to, Nathaniel would be a fine contender. Not because he is full of valour and genius for in that regard he’s the same as the next person, but because he’s a funny, cooky and intelligent melodramatasist whose talents are wasted on the benign.
Nazeem: Fascinating name for an enigmatic and funny bastard. For example, it’s easier to pronounce ‘Nazeem’ if you’re smiling, but in a rather bizarre dichotomy, it’s also wonderful to shout as a swear-replacement at 3am just after you’ve cracked your second smallest toes into a large, sharp toy en route to a barely-awake urination. So, yes, he’s funny, but he’s fucking frustrating as well. Weird thing is, we can’t even tell you why. We just don’t know. Nazeem
Nazomi: As a young child he was a first rate nightmare. Indeed, how his parents didn't throw him overboard on that trip I'm not sure. We would have. But, in adulthood, Nazomi has shed all that tantrum-throwing out the window and he actually takes his time and considers his position before acting. He might even consider others, and who would have imagined that 15 years ago?
Neal: Neal gets involved in his community. He’s got his first aid certificate, which he remembers every detail of, he helps old ladies cross the road and he has even volunteered for St.Vinnies. He eats well but not extravagantly, he likes a wee glass of port of an evening and at his funeral will be a large congregation, each of whom will be compelled to ask themselves how much they give. Thank you Neal.
Neale: Wise beyond his years, Neale is revered within his friendship group - a rather dignified and intelligent group - for being the most level-headed of them all, and this is no mean feat. He thinks before he speaks and is therefore a good listener. When it comes to romance he is attentive and caring, although he so content in his own company he sometimes forgets to pursue such things in the first place. He often has an indoor hobby.
Ned: Ned slips under the radar as an underrated, genuine and sufficiently hilarious legend. Shocking with women.
Negs: The Negs of adulthood is almost identical to the Negs of his childhood. In primary school, for instance, if he and his best mate were being chastised by the female teacher and most of the anger was directed at his mate, Negs would use the opportunity to sneak around behind the head mistress and gently lift up her skirt for a quick peek.
Neil: Neil rhymes with any decent grimace. (eg: pulling leeches from your skin, ripping the wax from a hirsute part of your body, extracting tropical ticks that have their heads embedded in you and running across 90 degree sand without sandals in order to get to the water.) But, he is a loving man who is true and loyal.
Nelly: A good honest worker who will gladly put himself in harms way in order to save the tribe.
Nelson: A deranged man who yells at non-existent people, who are caught up in his paranoid delusions of world catastrophe and bloodshed. Either that or he's a genius way ahead of his time. I guess we'll find out...
Nesh: Nesh is a happy, busy guy. He likes to dress in a stylish fashion, he is successful in work, he masturbates in front of the mirror, he is funny and he has friends. What more can a fellow ask for? He’s not tall.
Nev: You’ll often find him at the bar of any inland pub on a Friday afternoon drinking with a few of his mates.
Neville: Neville doesn’t like what the young folk are doing to the world, and he especially doesn’t like their lack of morals and manners. When he visits the dentist to have a tooth removed he refuses to have a local anaesthetic, and there’s no way he’d abandon a fruitful fishing trip if he accidentally stuck a hook through his thumb that went all the way through the nail.
Newt: Well (spit)…..somebody told me that if I rode this damn donkey out here and carried this bag (spit) for these people, that someone would pay me a lot of money (spit). But, hell, it's boiling hot, I ain't got no water, I can't seem to find the people I'm meant to be givin' this bag to (spit) and, shit, I might just die out here and no one'll know. How dumb would that be? (Excellent question, Newt.)
Newton: What it is with some men? Is he the dummest smart man on the planet? Yes, Newton, we know - you're maths skills are top of the class, you can sip a wine and tell us from which side of the valley it was made, let alone its vintage and country of origin and what you don't know about world politics isn't worth talking about, but why oh why would you get near the edge of a boat’s deck wearing rubber gum boots? If you fall in, by the time you get them off you'll be so far from the surface it won't matter. Like that other time you mowed the lawn in your bear feet and wonder how you ended up with 12 stitches. You with me?
Niall: A hard-working scientist who deals with wetlands. He spends most of his time in the lab, or so he says, anyway.
Nicholas: Giant IQ. Nicholas is a pale-skinned man with the demeanour of an arrogant used-car salesman. People befriend him because they feel bad that he doesn’t have any until they realise why he hasn’t got any. But, as a gifted shit-stirrer who gets off on testing others, he’s highly intelligent and you can’t begrudge him that.
Nick: The prodigal son that women are magnetically attracted to. Reckless and irresponsible, he loves outdoor sports and nightclubs, and he understands his place in the world, perfectly. He’s never filed a tax return in his life.
Nico: Possibly as bald as a fair dinkum badger, Nico pesters and is easily pestered, himself. He is well-dressed and he's always checking his wallet. He's certain that all women adore him, but there is a rumour his is actually crap in bed?....Can anyone confirm this for us?...
Nicolai: Works very hard. Saves his pennies. Encourages his kids to do the same. And when he drinks…..ooh, my goodness, does he drink!
Niels: He might be Austrian, then again his dad might have arrived here on a boat from Denmark 40 years ago. Where ever his blood originates from, however, Niels is a duty-filled man who devotes himself to any task.
Nigel: It’s not Nigel’s fault that he has idiotically rude parents, but you can forget the rumours because he is a far nicer and more intelligent person than we were led to believe. Indeed, Nigel is top notch.
Nike: Well I suppose they could have called him Toyota Corolla, or maybe, Northrop Grumman. But no, they called him Nike, and it's true, he can run abit, especially around tight little corners when the cops are after him.
Nikhil: Like a demanding gymnastics coach, Nikhil carries almost unrealistic expectations but you have to give him points for persistence.
Nikome: Nikome possesses the resting heart rate of an Olympic distance swimmer and the smile of a contented monk who has been reincarnated so many times that nothing surprises him anymore.
Nimrod: Ever seen the puppet TV show, The Avengers? Well Nimrod is the name of a Commander of a battleship whose job is to sail around the seas and randomly shoot its cannons into rogue states. There's no diplomacy here folks. "Let's just get in there and get those bad guys, even before they become bad guys": this is Nimrod's personal motto. Is he this demonstrative in the street or in the kitchen? Well, no, that's the weird thing. Around the house he's a big loveable pussy cat, but put him in a uniform and hand him some weapons then WOAH! Look out!
Nitram: While not a busy-body, Nitram is definitely a busy-beaver. He seems to have several projects on the go at the same time and this doesn’t faze him. The trade-off is that he can wake up some days and realise he hasn’t had any romance for years.
Nixon:
Nah, Nixon aint no mole in the ground. He's more like a giant bald eagle wearing flashy silver trousers, who soars through the sky shouting, "God-damn!! Look at me soar!!! Yeah!!!!"

You have no choice, therefore, but to love him.
Niz: Serene and truly good (like the fourth of fifth day after earth’s alleged creation when there were no animals or humans – just plants) Niz is the quiet calm of the thick rainforest that existed before the maelstrom of animal life and death that came later.
Noa: And bloody bravo mum and dad for ditching the h at the end. The boys in the commentary box have been discussing the two species of Noah/Noa for a while now, and everyone is scratching their heads. With the h ripped off Noa is now suddenly fast, he wants things to happen, he’s into life and movement, and yet he has achieved all this without his ego tearing off up the street like a flamingo with its nuts out. Noa is a man of the earth/water, no question, and if you own one our only advice is to not to pen him in or try to change him, ever. He may settle one day, but it has to be on his terms and in his time. Let us know how you go…
Noah: His name leaves your mouth and swirls around like a puff of disappearing smoke and Noah is therefore hard to get to know, but he is an intense soul who thinks a hell of a lot and he comes from a generation that feel entitled to be blissfully happy 24/7. (Note: 57% of the time Noah is an aspiring artist, he wears lots of black and loves being viewed as something of a hipster, though he’d never admit it).
Noak: Noak, are you Australian, firstly, and if not, have you heard of it? In case you haven't there's a phrase they have down there called 'blue balls'. It's a condition that I won't go into here. If you don't know what it is I suggest you look it up. And then, do something about it. You'll be surprised how much girls will want to talk to you. Management.
Noam:
“Do you know what your values are and are you being fair?” 
These are questions Noam might ask you and if you answer yes, he will expect you to break the rules but only in accordance with fairness, not greed.
Noel: It happens to men more than women I think, but ‘Noel’ is the name of the rather tragic splash that occurs whenever a mobile phone is accidentally dropped into the dunny while a person is taking a piss.
Nolan: Rarely first out of the blocks, Nolan isn’t one for physical exertion, which is a pity. Indeed, it’s about the only advice the commentary team can offer him. He’s certainly educated enough.
Nor: Nor will quite happily walk into a busy pub on his own, enjoy a beer or three, and be completely unfazed whether he ends up speaking to everyone or no one.
Norm: Norm rarely showers, which is a pity because he lives in the heat of Northern Australia, Southern Florida or perhaps the Philippines, and he only moves quickly when he needs to grab another beer although he’ll do anything for anybody, if asked. (He’d never tell you, openly, but he craves the company.)
Norman: Richard’s offsider and a fellow knight, who is blessed with no common sense whatsoever. The last time he rode into battle he accidentally stabbed his own horse with his sword as they were crossing a stream. The poor horse died and Norman, the irreverent twit, damn-near drowned in the process.
Nugget: Nugget is the working-mans’ ideal of a funny little bastard and if he isn’t very short, he’s a certainty to have a bright red afro.
Nusque: Forget his heritage in this life. In a past life, in fact in a few past lives, Nusque was an Eskimo living way up in the northern hemisphere. First world hardships, dramas and smartphone meltdowns mean nothing to him because he's done it way tougher than most of these fools, here in the west, here in the 21st century. He's warmed by weird humour as well, and as such his friends are quite remarkable, also. Nusque is very comfortable in his skin, which, let's face it, is most of the battle. Nice work Nusque.
Nuts: It’s not possible to be called Nuts and not be a humorous individual but the ego, which in this case runs far deeper than the larrikin at the surface, will always get things done in the end.
Nye: Traffic cop. He can stand in one spot, uncomplaining, for days.
